recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Bowl
ing: ~6 oz of the plain shredded chicken from the Monday bake (the tray makes two bowls)
1 microwave rice pouch
2 tbsp buffalo sauce · 2 tbsp Greek yogurt · 0.5 oz shredded cheddar
Shredded carrots, sliced celery, scallions

steps.t: Take about 6 oz of the plain shredded chicken out of the fridge.
Toss it with the buffalo sauce until every shred is coated. Do this cold — the sauce clings better than it does on hot chicken.
Rice pouch in the microwave.
Rice down, buffalo chicken on top, then carrots, celery, yogurt, cheddar, and scallions.

recipes.note: This is the week’s insurance policy. On a night when nothing is prepped and you do not want to cook, it is five minutes of assembly and 65g of protein — because Monday already did the cooking.

recipes.name: Dump-and-Bake Salsa Chicken
ing: 1.5 lbs chicken breasts for the salsa dish
1 lb chicken breasts, plain (these become two buffalo bowls — see step 2)
1 jar chunky salsa
3 oz shredded cheddar
2 microwave rice pouches
Greek yogurt and lime to finish

steps.t: Oven to 400°F. Put 1.5 lbs of chicken in a baking dish and pour the entire jar of salsa over it. No seasoning, no oil, no browning. That is the whole prep.
Put the other 1 lb on a foil-lined tray, salt and pepper, nothing else. Both go in together — same oven, same 25 minutes, no extra work.
Bake 25 min, until both hit 165°F.
Shred the salsa chicken with two forks right in the dish so the meat drinks the salsa back up. This is the step that makes it taste like something.
Cheddar over the salsa dish, back in the oven 3 min to melt.
Shred the plain tray separately and container it — that is two buffalo bowls for later in the week.
Boil the eggs now while the oven is still hot. Microwave the rice. Three containers of salsa chicken.

recipes.note: Two trays, one oven, one timer. The plain tray costs you nothing but a sheet of foil, and it means the buffalo bowls later in the week are pure assembly with no cooking at all.

recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage, Peppers & Potatoes
ing: 2 packs chicken sausage, sliced into thick coins
3 bell peppers (use three different colors), thick strips
1 red onion, wedges
1.5 lbs baby potatoes, halved
1 tbsp olive oil · Italian seasoning · garlic powder

steps.t: Oven to 425°F. Potatoes cut-side down with the oil, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Roast 15 min alone — they need the head start.
Meanwhile slice the sausage and peppers thick. Thick, not thin — thin strips go limp and disappear.
Everything onto the pan, toss once, back in for 18 min. Pull it when the pepper edges char. Those blackened edges are where the flavor is.
Three containers.

recipes.note: Three colors of pepper, not three of the same. Costs the same and it is the difference between a meal you look forward to and a beige tray — which is exactly what went wrong with last week’s stir-fry.

recipes.name: Protein Mac & Cheese
ing: 1.25 lbs ground beef 93/7
6 oz elbow pasta
1.5 cups cottage cheese
4 oz shredded cheddar · splash of Fairlife milk
1 tsp Dijon · garlic powder · onion powder · smoked paprika

steps.t: Pasta into boiling salted water, 10 min.
While it boils: beef in a skillet over medium-high, break it up, cook until no pink, ~7 min. Salt it well.

Blend the cottage cheese with the milk, Dijon, and spices until it is completely smooth. This is the entire trick — blended it becomes a silky cheese sauce, unblended it stays grainy and you will not make it twice.
Drain the pasta, back into the pot off the heat. Stir in the blended cottage cheese, then the cheddar, until it melts into a sauce.
Fold in the beef. Three containers.

recipes.note: Cottage cheese is doing the work of a butter-and-flour roux here. Same creamy sauce, but the base carries 12g of protein per serving instead of none — which is how mac and cheese ends up at 59g a portion.
